description: Targeted probe of genuine failure patterns

results.prompt: The hi-hats are playing 32nd notes flat out, but the kick and snare are barely there
The hi-hats drive constant 16th notes while the kick lands heavy on one and three and the snare hits two and four
The kick hits hard on the downbeat while the hi-hats keep a steady eighth pulse and the snare cracks on the backbeat
The snare has a heavy shuffle swing to it, and the hi-hats follow that same lilt with tight 16th notes
The ride cymbal keeps steady time, the hi-hats accent the offbeats with sharp bursts, and the crash punctuates the downbeat
The kick drum has almost no swing — it's totally straight, machine-like — while the hi-hats swing hard against it
The toms cascade down into the downbeat with a loose, sloppy timing while the hi-hats stay tight and precise
The harmony is built on stacked fourths — those perfect fourths create an open, suspended quality in the voicings
The left hand plays power chords with lots of fifths while the right hand runs up in stepwise motion
The melody uses a lot of tritone leaps — really angular, jarring — while the harmony underneath stays on close-position clusters
The vocal line is full of octave jumps — it leaps up and then back down — with the pads underneath holding sustained fifths
Chromatic half-step descents in the bass while the chords above move in minor thirds — really dark and close
The melody stays mostly stepwise — small intervals — but the harmony underneath jumps around with big skips of sixths and sevenths
The kick drum is absolutely relentless — hammering every quarter note with maximum force
The crash cymbal crashes down on every downbeat — it's the main structural marker of the whole groove
The snare is barely audible — a tiny ghost note that's almost lost in the mix
The hi-hats are incredibly dense — constant 32nd notes that never let up
Everything is extremely quiet, restrained — the whole kit sounds like it's being played with brushes from another room
The open hi-hats ring out for incredibly long stretches — they barely close at all
The hi-hat sound is almost nonexistent — you can barely hear it, but the ride carries the time
The cymbals are dominated by the crash accents — the hi-hats are just there, nothing special
The ride cymbal keeps a steady pattern throughout, the hi-hats chime in occasionally with open accents, and the crash never appears
All hi-hat all the time — both open and closed — with the occasional splash accent
The snare absolutely nails the backbeat every single time — rock solid
The kick tries to hit the one and three but keeps missing — really sloppy drummer
The snare ghost notes on offbeats are perfectly placed every time, but the main backbeat hit is sloppy
The hi-hats play straight eight notes with no swing at all, while the kick bounces on the swing
The note starts are extremely close together — everything sounds like a single percussive burst
The spacing is really open — notes start far apart, mostly whole notes or more between attacks
The texture alternates between sparse single notes and thick 6-plus-note clusters
Everything is sustained for a very long time — notes overlap for bars and bars
Most of the sounds are really short — staccato eighth note bursts separated by silence
The chords are huge — six or more notes in every voicing — really dense and complex
